data.mounting_note: Catalog-level fact: every unit in the wall chapter hangs. HOW HIGH is a project decision and lives in Standards::WALL_MOUNT_BOTTOM_MM until M1.6.
data.n_elle_note: The elevation carries 'N Elle' at 86,2 = 84 + 2,2. RECORDED, NOT IMPLEMENTED. CORRECTION 2026-08-23, evening (learned rule 9 - added, not erased): THIS FIGURE IS NOT PRINTED ON THE PAGE. pdftotext -bbox puts 'N- Elle' at a normal 7,5 pt over the perspective drawing on every wall page of this chapter; rendering exactly that box at 400 and at 600 dpi shows blank paper. It is white text, or a hidden layer for the N_Elle edition - IN THE FILE, NOT IN THE BOOK. The wording above ('the elevation carries', 'the second elevation on this page') is therefore wrong, and the H.48 note's guess that the 170-dpi render merely lacked resolution is wrong too. THE NUMBER STAYS, RELABELLED: a document lead BELOW source trust, used for nothing and not to be quoted to Elda as something the catalog prints. Learned rule 10 says the render is the page; this is the first time the text layer claimed something the page does not, and it will not be the last.
page_observations: THE STACK IS UNEQUAL HERE - 48 ON TOP, 36 BELOW. H.72 splits its two-leaf types 36 + 36; H.84 splits them 48 + 36, and the elevation dimensions both. So a stacked pair is NOT two halves of the family height: it is two stated heights that happen to sum to it. Anything that derives the split by dividing by two is wrong at this family and right at the last one.

AND THE CATALOG'S WORDING CHANGES WITH IT. H.72 prints '2 top-hung doors' and '2 doors'; H.84 prints '1 top-hung door' TWICE and '1 door' twice, on separate lines. Two equal leaves get one plural line, two unequal leaves get one line each. A wording difference that tracks a dimensional one is worth trusting.

THE MICROWAVE-NICHE UNIT IS THE SECTION HEIGHT MINUS 360, TWICE NOW. PE0696 is 360 inside the H.72 section, PG0696 is 480 inside the H.84 section. TWO INSTANCES, so it is recorded as an observation and NOT relied on: the third family that prints one will say whether it is a rule.
THE FOLDING TYPE STOPS AT W.90 - four widths, where H.72 has six and runs to 120. Its compound, by contrast, has THREE codes here against H.72's one.
The two boiler housings are d.62, exactly as at H.72, and carry 'custom-sized side panels' the same way. Two families now agree on that.
The one-door type gains a second shelf: H.72 prints '1 shelf', H.84 prints '2 shelves' for the same position.

wall_pull_out_door.description: Wall unit with pull-out door - 1 door - 1 soft-close pull-out door - no Push-pull device
wall_pull_out_door.notes: Same single W.15 code as H.72, same suffix 30. The catalog spells the last line 'no Push-pull device' here and 'no push-pull' at H.72; the description keeps each page's own wording.

front_layout.note: One full-height front on a pull-out mechanism. NO hinge_axis and no open_leaf - the travel is not in the catalog.

wall_door.description: Wall unit with door - 1 rh or lh door - 2 shelves
wall_door.notes: Four widths, the same set as H.72. TWO shelves where H.72 has one - a taller box takes another. ONE CODE, BOTH HANDS.

front_layout.note: One door covering the full front, hinged on a vertical edge. hinge_side per order.

wall_two_doors.description: Wall unit with doors - 2 doors - 2 shelves

front_layout.note: Two doors meeting in the middle.

wall_top_hung_doors_stacked.description: Wall unit with top-hung doors - 1 top-hung door - 1 top-hung door - 1 shelf - top door with Push-pull device
wall_top_hung_doors_stacked.notes: TWO LEAVES OF DIFFERENT SIZES - 480 above, 360 below, both dimensioned on the elevation and summing to 840. Only the TOP door carries a Push-pull device. Suffix 04, the same digits that mean a side-by-side compound at H.48 and H.60 and an EQUAL stacked pair at H.72.

front_layout.note: 480 then 360, summing to the family's 840. NO hinge_axis: one key cannot carry two leaves, and here they are not even the same size. Slabs are correct - two of them, which is also the handle count.

wall_folding_doors.description: Wall unit with horizontally folding doors - 1 door - 1 door - 2 shelves - interior Valencia handle - no Push-pull device
wall_folding_doors.notes: FOUR widths, stopping at 90. H.72 has six and runs to 120. Suffix 89 in both families.

front_layout.note: 480 then 360. NO hinge_axis and no mechanism figure - a folding pair moves in a way this catalog has not dimensioned.

wall_compound_2_folding.description: Wall unit with horizontally folding doors - 1 door - 1 door - 4 shelves - interior Valencia handle - no Push-pull device
wall_compound_2_folding.notes: THREE codes where H.72 has one, and it keeps the same heading as the simple type - the word 'Compound' appears nowhere on this position; the module splits are what identify it. Four shelves against the simple type's two, one pair per module.
